text.p: Olympic officials will not be able to reveal the result of an investigation into alleged corruption among 1988 Seoul Games boxing judges until May because they need to interview one key figure in the affair.

The IOC appointed a commission to investigate allegations that American light-middleweight Roy Jones was cheated out of a gold medal by bribed judges and was expected to announce the result of its findings this month.
But IOC director general Francois Carrard said on Monday: "We expect to have a final report in May. The working group wants to have a hearing with one person."
Jones, who went on to become a professional world champion, was beaten in the 1988 final by South Korean Park Si-hun after an extraordinary decision.
Most spectators and commentators present had Jones way ahead of his outclassed opponent but three judges from Morocco, Uruguay and Uganda gave the decision to Park.
